title: Evaluation of a low-threshold intervention programme for secondary individual prevention of back pain
summary:
Back problems are a common cause of sick leave across all workplaces. Early, preventive treatment of back problems is therefore an important measure against incapacity for work.
The aim of the study is to find out whether a short-term preventive training programme can bring about a lasting improvement in back problems among employees at the BG Klinikum Duisburg. Before the start (T0) of the training intervention, back problems and general quality of life are assessed using questionnaires and the strength of the back muscles is measured.
This is followed by guided group training twice a week over a period of three months.
After completion of the training intervention, the questionnaires are filled out again and the strength of the back muscles is measured (T1) to determine the success of the training. Finally, after six months (T2), the questionnaires are filled out one last time and the strength of the back muscles is measured to determine the long-term success of the training.
conditions: self-reported back pain and back problems

interventions.name: Employees who report back problems participate in group training twice a week for three months. Inclusion criteria:
- Employees of BG Klinikum Duisburg
- Existing self-reported back pain
- Written consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Previous disc herniations
- Refusal to participate in the study
- Insufficient knowledge of German
